title: The coalition structure core is accessible
abstract: For each outcome (i.e. a payoff vector augmented with a coalition structure) of a TU-game with a non-empty coalition structure core there exists a finite sequence of successively dominating outcomes that terminates in the coalition structure core. In order to obtain this result a restrictive dominance relation — which we label outsider independent — is employed.
summary_en: In a transferable-utility game with a non-empty coalition-structure core, every payoff outcome can be reached through a finite sequence of successive dominations. Kóczy and Lauwers prove this accessibility result using a restricted dominance concept ('outsider independent') that requires non-blocking coalitions to keep their payoffs unchanged. The result formalises the intuition that bargaining processes converge in finite time to coalition-structure cores, providing a procedural foundation for the static solution concept.
data_used: Theoretical model — TU-game accessibility analysis. No primary dataset.
policy_relevance: Foundational result supporting the use of coalition-structure-core analysis in policy settings (intergovernmental bargaining, European Council seat allocation, EU institutional coalition formation). Provides theoretical assurance that core outcomes can be reached through realistic bargaining processes.
